summary: Intermittent SSE resume trims base64-encoded inline images and omits stream terminator behind corporate WAF
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long streaming responses containing inline base64-encoded image attachments are sometimes truncated after a brief reconnect. The final stream terminator (closing JSON event) is missing, and the embedded image payload is cut mid-chunk, resulting in a corrupt image on the client. Impact: Synthetic Health's docs generator drops images intermittently in production for a subset of users behind their corporate WAF/proxy; they see ~2-3% of SSE sessions truncated during resume windows. Environment: prod-us-east, our hosted API via edge-proxy cluster behind FastGate WAF. Frequency: intermittent, observed during bursts and during auth token refreshes. Observed behavior: initial SSE stream emits ~80KB of text plus a ~120KB base64 image embedded as part of the final event. During a reconnect/resume (client attempts resume after a short TCP/TLS disconnect), the resumed stream returns earlier chunks but the base64 payload is missing its last 10-15 KB and the final "event: done" marker is not delivered. Client shows parse error (unterminated string).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a streaming request that produces a final event containing a base64-encoded PNG (~100-200KB) as part of the JSON payload.
2) Start streaming via SSE from the hosted API through the enterprise WAF (FastGate) in front of customer network.
3) Mid-stream, simulate a brief TCP/TLS disruption (client network toggle or short NAT timeout) causing the client to reconnect and resume using the last seen event-offset header.
4) Observe resumed stream: look for missing trailing bytes from the base64 payload and absence of the terminal event marker.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-01 15:40 - Replayed sample trace from Synthium (trace id: trace-8234). Upstream serving runtime reports final_event_sent=true in logs, but edge-proxy shows truncated payload delivered to client after WAF interaction.
2026-03-01 16:05 - FastGate WAF logs indicate chunk coalescing/rewrite for large SSE frames; WAF inserted a keepalive probe during resume sequence (see waf_id: FG-12-20260301).

2026-03-01 16:30 - Hypothesis: WAF/edge-proxy interplay is dropping trailing bytes when resume happens and the proxy is rewriting Content-Encoding/Transfer semantics. The content-length-like framing for SSE resumes is relying on application-level offsets; an intermediary coalesce or chunk rewrite loses last partial chunk boundary leading client to miss terminator event.

2026-03-02 09:12 - Reproduced in staging using in-house WAF appliance with configured coalescing: resume after token refresh produces truncated base64 embed in 3/10 attempts when WAF coalescing enabled; 0/10 when bypassing WAF.
comments: Maya Patel (Support) 2026-03-01: Received initial report from Synthium Support engineer. Customer reproduced with reproducible harness and attached traces. Assigned to Jonah for deep-dive.

Jonah Kim (SRE) 2026-03-01: I pulled the traces. serving-runtime shows payload fully emitted and final 'done' event flagged. Edge-proxy log shows downstream broken_pipe and truncated bytes. Raising red flag on WAF coalescing/transfer handling.

Customer (Synthium) 2026-03-01: Confirmed that bypassing their corporate WAF (direct to our public endpoint) resolves the issue; images are intact. They cannot turn off WAF in production long-term. Requesting workaround and fix timeline.

Jonah Kim (SRE) 2026-03-02: Temporary mitigation: enabling 'preserve-chunk-boundaries' feature flag on edge-proxy cluster for the affected VIP reduced truncation to 0/20 in internal tests. Planning patch to ensure resume respects application-level offsets even when intermediary rewrites occur.

Engineering (Edge Team) 2026-03-02: Working on PR to add explicit resume offset header validation and to keep a small trailing-buffer flush before closing downstream socket to allow WAF to complete any in-flight coalescing. PR drafted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/877
resolution: Workaround applied: enabled preserve-chunk-boundaries flag for synthium's tenant on edge-proxy VIP and coordinated a temporary bypass of WAF coalescing rule. Deployed hotfix to edge-proxy that adds a 200ms trailing flush and validates resume-offset against serving-runtime commit sequence. Root cause: edge-proxy + WAF coalescing could drop the terminal partial chunk during resume handoff, removing the final JSON event terminator and truncating base64 payload. Fix merged to main (PR #877) and scheduled for staged rollout on 2026-03-05. Customer informed and asked to test. Follow-up: add additional unit/e2e tests for SSE resume with large inline blobs and document recommended WAF rules in SSE Runbook.
follow_up_actions: 1) QA: add e2e test harness for SSE resume with >100KB inline attachments (owner: QA).
2) Docs: update SSE Runbook with 'WAF configuration recommendations' and 'edge-proxy preserve-chunk-boundaries flag' (owner: Developer Experience).
3) Product: consider exposing resume-offset diagnostics to customers as header in response for easier debugging (owner: API Product).
4) Postmortem: schedule internal postmortem if customer sees further incidents after staged rollout (owner: SRE).
